description: Ground-truth vulnerability list for the lending.rs (CosmWasm) eval fixture. A finding 'counts' as matching one of these only if it identifies the same location AND the same underlying issue. Use with evals/evals.json eval #2 and EVAL-METHODOLOGY.md's Layer 3 scoring.

vulnerabilities.description: `amount` is never checked against DEPOSITS[info.sender] (or any per-user record) before being subtracted from cfg.total_deposits — any caller can call Withdraw with an arbitrary amount and it will be accepted, corrupting the contract's global accounting state regardless of what that caller actually deposited. Compounding this: execute_withdraw never updates the DEPOSITS map at all (only deposit() does), so even a naive per-user check added later would need a second, separate bug fixed alongside it.
vulnerabilities.why_planted: The most severe finding — mirrors LEND-1 in the Solana fixture and POOL-3-adjacent business-logic-gap findings in the EVM fixture, deliberately, to test whether an audit catches this class of bug consistently across chains rather than only when it matches a chain-specific checklist item verbatim.

verified.method: Confirmed by inspection: execute_withdraw() reads `amount` directly from the ExecuteMsg with no lookup against DEPOSITS.load(deps.storage, &info.sender) anywhere in the function body — directly readable, not inferred.

fail_to_pass.description: cw-multitest integration test: a caller who never deposited anything calls Withdraw with an arbitrary amount. Tests the REAL invariant — that the contract's recorded total_deposits accounting cannot be corrupted by a caller with no recorded deposit — not just 'did the call return an error', per the SWE-ABS lesson.
fail_to_pass.expected_before_fix: FAILS — the call succeeds and total_deposits drops by 1000 even though the attacker never deposited anything.
fail_to_pass.expected_after_fix: PASSES once execute_withdraw() loads DEPOSITS[info.sender], checks amount against it, and rejects the call for an attacker with no recorded deposit (or a deposit smaller than the requested amount).

vulnerabilities.pass_to_pass: An honest depositor withdrawing an amount they actually deposited must continue to succeed after any fix — a fix that blocks all withdrawals is not an acceptable fix.

vulnerabilities.location: execute_deposit() line 49 (`cfg.total_deposits += sent`) and execute_withdraw() line 66 (`cfg.total_deposits - amount`)
vulnerabilities.description: Both use raw operators instead of `checked_add`/`checked_sub` on Uint128, contrary to references/coding-standards.md's explicit rule. Uint128's arithmetic panics on overflow/underflow rather than silently wrapping, so this isn't a silent-wrap vulnerability, but it is still a correctness/DoS concern (an uncontrolled panic aborts the tx with a less informative error than an explicit checked-op's typed error) and a direct violation of this suite's own stated coding standard for the chain.
vulnerabilities.why_planted: Tests whether 'unchecked arithmetic' findings are reported even when the concrete exploit impact is more about error-handling quality than direct fund loss — distinguishing this from CWLEND-1, which does have direct fund/accounting-integrity impact.

vulnerabilities.location: execute_withdraw(), entire function — DEPOSITS map never touched
vulnerabilities.description: deposit() updates both CONFIG.total_deposits and DEPOSITS[sender]; withdraw() only updates CONFIG.total_deposits, never DEPOSITS[sender]. Even independent of CWLEND-1, this means the two storage structures can never be reconciled — DEPOSITS becomes a monotonically-increasing-only record that no longer reflects actual outstanding balances after any withdrawal.
vulnerabilities.why_planted: Tests whether an audit reasons about state *consistency* across the full set of storage-mutating branches, not just each branch's arithmetic in isolation — a distinct skill from CWLEND-1/2.

not_a_vulnerability_but_might_be_flagged.note: There's no BankMsg::Send anywhere in execute_withdraw — funds never actually leave the contract's bank balance despite the accounting change. This is arguably a functional bug (withdraw doesn't work) more than a security vulnerability per se, since it doesn't enable fund theft — it just means the fixture's accounting can be corrupted without real-world fund loss as written. An audit that flags this as informational/low ('withdraw doesn't transfer funds — likely incomplete rather than exploitable') should be treated as a correct, bonus observation, not scored against CWLEND-1/2/3.
